title: Bilinearity of derived completed tensor and its rational Hom action
statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a site small relative to a coefficient universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $A$ a commutative ring, and $s:A\to\Gamma(\mathcal S,R)$ a unital homomorphism. Give module-sheaf Hom groups and their unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-linear-category] the induced $A$-linear structures. Let $T:D(R)\times D(R)\to D(R)$ be the specified derived tensor obtained by localization of signed total sheaf tensor on flat-term K-flat homotopy representatives [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Fix a finite list of global sections of $R$, and let $L:D(R)\to\mathcal C$ be its Koszul completion reflector with natural unit $\eta$, where $\mathcal C$ is the full subcategory of complete objects [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]. Write $B(M,N)=L(T(M,N))$ for $M,N\in\mathcal C$.

The functor $L$ is additive and $A$-linear; each of $T$ and $B$ is additive and $A$-linear separately in both variables. For $p\in A$, put $S=A[1/p]$ and use raw scalar localization $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/p]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For every $M,M',N,N'\in\mathcal C$ there is a unique $S$-bilinear map
$$\beta_{M,M',N,N'}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C[1/p]}(M,M')\times\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C[1/p]}(N,N')\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C[1/p]}(B(M,N),B(M',N'))$$
satisfying $\beta(x\otimes f,y\otimes g)=xy\otimes B(f,g)$ for $x,y\in S$ and integral morphisms $f,g$, writing the scalar factor first. These maps preserve identities and simultaneous composition, hence with object map $B$ define a bifunctor $\bar B$ on $\mathcal C[1/p]$. In particular $\bar B(f/p^r,g/p^t)=B(f,g)/p^{r+t}$, without any torsion-freeness assumption.

proof.text: On a module-sheaf Hom group define $(af)_U(x)=s(a)|_U f_U(x)$; restriction compatibility follows from the restriction rule in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Composition is bilinear by componentwise calculation. The same formulas on chain maps give an $A$-linear category of complexes. For the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $((af+bf')\otimes g)(x\otimes y)=s(a)f(x)\otimes g(y)+s(b)f'(x)\otimes g(y)$ sectionwise before sheafification; the balancing relation moves either scalar to the output. Equality passes through sheafification, and the other variable has the same formula. On each summand of the signed direct-sum totalization [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] the induced chain map is $f^i\otimes g^j$. Thus total tensor on complexes preserves sums and scalar multiplication separately: its fixed signs in the differential do not change these equalities.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor followed by sheafification; explicit componentwise calculation

proof.text: Write $q:\mathrm{CoCh}(R)\to D(R)$ for the localization at quasi-isomorphisms in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It is additive by [lem-sfb-derived-localization-additive]. Apply [lem-sfb-additive-localization-linear] to the $A$-linear complex category of Step 1, this additive localization, and the preadditive derived category. This gives exactly the induced $A$-linear structure on $D(R)$ and makes $q$ $A$-linear. Thus $q$ preserves both sums and scalar multiplication on all chain maps.

source.place: Definition 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category), additive localization; scalar structure via the cited Mathlib localization leaf

proof.text: Fix a flat-term K-flat complex $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], the total-tensor functors with fixed factor $P$ descend to exact, hence additive, functors $G_P,H_P:D(R)\to D(R)$ canonically identified with $T(qP,-)$ and $T(-,qP)$. Their descent comparisons identify $G_Pq$ with $q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes-)$ and $H_Pq$ with $q\operatorname{Tot}(-\otimes P)$. The latter functors are additive and $A$-linear by Steps 1–2. Apply [lem-sfb-linear-localization-descent] to $q$ and each comparison: $G_P$ and $H_P$ preserve scalar multiplication as well. The equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] supplies for every derived object $M$ a flat-term K-flat $P$ and an isomorphism $e:qP\cong M$. Bifunctoriality gives natural isomorphisms $T(e,1):T(qP,-)\cong T(M,-)$ and $T(1,e):T(-,qP)\cong T(-,M)$. Conjugating any sum or scalar multiple by an isomorphism preserves it, since composition is $A$-bilinear. Therefore both fixed-variable functors of $T$ are additive and $A$-linear for every $M$, independently of the chosen representative.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction); linear descent is the cited localization leaf

proof.text:
The full subcategory $\mathcal C$ inherits the Hom modules and bilinear composition of $D(R)$ [def-weil-linear-category]. For $f,f':X\to Y$ and $a,b\in A$, naturality of the unit gives
$$\bigl(aL(f)+bL(f')\bigr)\eta_X=\eta_Y(af+bf')=L(af+bf')\eta_X.$$
Here $LY$ is complete. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], with source $X$ and complete target $LY$, makes precomposition with $\eta_X$ injective on $\operatorname{Hom}(LX,LY)$. Hence $L(af+bf')=aL(f)+bL(f')$. This proves additivity and $A$-linearity of the specified reflector directly from its natural universal unit; it does not require a choice of a linear resolution functor.

Restrict $T$ to $\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$ and compose with $L$. Since both fixed-variable functors of $T$ and $L$ preserve sums and scalars, those of $B=L\circ T$ do also. Its simultaneous morphism action is
$$B(f,g)=B(1_{M'},g)\circ B(f,1_N)\quad(f:M\to M',\ g:N\to N').$$
Thus this action is $A$-bilinear, by the separate linearity just proved and bilinearity of composition [def-weil-linear-category]. As a composite of functors it preserves identities and simultaneous composition.

proof.text: For the four fixed objects apply the bilinear base-change clause of [def-weil-module-base-change] to the $A$-bilinear map $(f,g)\mapsto B(f,g)$ of Step 5 and the ring map $A\to S=A[1/p]$. It supplies a unique $S$-bilinear map on the two base-changed Hom modules with $(f\otimes x,g\otimes y)\mapsto B(f,g)\otimes xy$. By [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] these are precisely the raw localized Hom modules. The notation in the item puts the scalar first: $x\otimes f$ denotes $f\otimes x$ under the canonical tensor flip, and $xy\otimes B(f,g)$ denotes $B(f,g)\otimes xy$. Therefore the resulting map is exactly $\beta$ with its required formula and uniqueness. The cited base-change assertion imposes no flatness or torsion-freeness condition on the Hom modules.

source.place: Section 00CV (section-tensor-product), Lemma 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), and Definition 05G4 (definition-base-change); the cited Mathlib base-change leaf supplies the bilinear extension

proof.text:
Use the composition and identity formula of [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-category]. First $\beta(1\otimes1_M,1\otimes1_N)=1\otimes1_{B(M,N)}$. For integral composable $f_1,f_2$ and $g_1,g_2$ and scalars $x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2\in S$, both the composite of their two $\beta$-images and the $\beta$-image of their simultaneous composites equal
$$(x_2y_2x_1y_1)\otimes B(f_2f_1,g_2g_1),$$
because $B(f_2,g_2)B(f_1,g_1)=B(f_2f_1,g_2g_1)$ and $S$ is commutative. Each side is $S$-multilinear in the four localized arrows. Every tensor element is a finite sum of pure tensors, so distributing proves the same equation for arbitrary arrows. Thus the maps define the claimed bifunctor with object map $B$. Taking $x=p^{-r}$, $y=p^{-t}$ in Step 6 gives $\bar B(f/p^r,g/p^t)=B(f,g)/p^{r+t}$. No cancellation of a power of $p$ was used, so this also covers torsion, zero localized Hom modules, and $S=0$.
